subject: [Prop Digest] Rightmove's £1.5bn case: now we wait
opener: Rightmove's legal fight just went to the judges, landlords are getting more arrears, and Nationwide is doing the opposite of what you'd expect with rates. Coffee up, let's go.

stories.text: The hearing on the £1.5bn legal action against Rightmove has finished, and the tribunal is holding its decision. A ruling on whether the claim proceeds, and how, is due in a few months. Property Industry EYE says around 13,000 agents are waiting on it. **Why it matters:** this is the first real test of whether the portal's position holds up against the agents who pay to be on it. **My take:** a few months is a long time for the rest of the industry to sit on its hands, so expect plenty of noise in the meantime.
stories.headline: Tribunal reserves judgement as Rightmove legal hearing ends

stories.text: Rent arrears are up 50% since the Renters’ Rights Act came in, according to Property Industry EYE. The piece says landlords are facing growing financial exposure. **Why it matters:** if arrears keep climbing, the cost of the new rules lands on landlords first, and agents managing their books will be the ones taking the calls.
stories.headline: Rent arrears surge 50% in wake of Renters’ Rights Act

stories.text: UK rents rose in October, but void periods surged, which Property Industry EYE reads as the rental market starting to slow. **Why it matters:** rent growth is still positive, but empty homes are where agents' fees disappear. Watch voids more than headline rents from here.
stories.headline: Rents keep climbing, but warning signs emerge for letting agents

stories.text: Goodlord’s latest Rental Index shows rent growth slowing and voids increasing as the market moves into its quieter period. **Why it matters:** this lines up with the October figures, so it's not a one-off blip.
stories.headline: Rental market enters its “winter cool down”

stories.text: Chestertons has reopened its dedicated sales operation, nine years after folding it into the wider business. **Why it matters:** a rare U-turn in a sector that usually just keeps merging. Whether it works will depend on how much the split costs them.
stories.headline: Chestertons reverses sales merger after nine years

stories.text: Nationwide's Carlo Pileggi says market conditions let the lender cut its fixed rates, even as tracker rates go up. **Why it matters:** if you're on a tracker, that's your cue to check your deal and ask what you're actually paying.
stories.headline: Nationwide says market allows fixed-rate cuts as trackers rise

stories.text: Caspar Harvard-Walls, who has worked at Foxtons and Black Brick, has launched Oskar. He says it helps house hunters find on- and off-market homes that fit their exact needs. **Why it matters:** off-market listings are where agents have always kept their edge, so a tool that goes hunting for them is worth a sideways look.
stories.headline: Former agent launches AI-powered home buying tool

stories.text: Supa, led by Upad founder Calum Brannan, has raised £21m. It plans to spend the money buying more market share through managing agent acquisitions. **Why it matters:** it's a roll-up playbook, and it's the same one that's been reshaping lettings agency for years.
stories.headline: Block management proptech raises £21m to disrupt ‘inefficient’ sector

stories.text: A study for the Home Builders Federation finds viability challenges are delaying or halting work for more than 60% of smaller housebuilders. Those firms are also buying fewer new sites and cutting staff. **Why it matters:** fewer small builders means fewer homes in the pipeline.
stories.headline: Viability problems stall work for over 60% of SME housebuilders
Thirdfort says compliance teams are under more pressure but still reluctant to fully adopt AI.
